title: Where Sam Bankman-Fried's Case Stands Now (2026)

lines.say: In twenty twenty-four, Sam Bankman-Fried was sentenced to twenty-five years for the FTX fraud.
lines.show: In 2024, Sam Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years for the FTX fraud.

lines.say: In April twenty twenty-six, the trial judge denied his bid for a new trial, calling his claim of government threats wildly conspiratorial.
lines.show: In April 2026, the trial judge denied his bid for a new trial, calling his claim of government threats "wildly conspiratorial."

lines.say: In June, the Second Circuit affirmed. The evidence, it said, was overwhelming.
He has asked President Trump for a pardon. According to news reports, Trump has said he has no plans to grant one. None has been granted.
In September, he asked the Supreme Court to hear his case. As this video was made, that petition was pending.
Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
